profile.reading: Digital Fortress Portland 2, facility code PTL2, is a Digital Fortress data center in Beaverton, Oregon, about 15 minutes from downtown Portland. Digital Fortress's own dedicated page for this facility, fetched directly from digital-fortress.com, describes a 3,500 square foot facility with 1.2 megawatts of available power on an N+1 concurrently maintainable configuration, 160 tons of DX cooling capacity, and hot aisle and cold aisle containment. The operator's own page lists SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II compliance, membership in the Northwest Access Exchange (NWAX), connectivity to 16 fiber optic carriers and seven subsea cables, and connectivity to the Seattle Internet Exchange (SIX). A third party aggregator, DataCenterMap, independently lists this same building's power capacity as 1.2 MW, matching the operator's own figure. A Digital Fortress press release, also fetched directly from the operator's own site, dated January 19, 2021, documents that Digital Fortress acquired this facility along with two sibling buildings in this registry, downtown Portland 1 and neighboring Portland 3 roughly 50 meters away, from Atmosera Inc.'s colocation business, transferring more than 100 colocation customers in the deal. This registry's own stored street address, 9705 Southwest Sunshine Court, Beaverton, Oregon, comes from a reverse geocode of the stored coordinates rather than a Digital Fortress primary source, though the immediately neighboring Portland 3 building's own reverse geocoded address on Sunshine Court is independently corroborated by a datacenterHawk listing for that sibling facility, lending some indirect support to the accuracy of this row's address as well. Digital Fortress is a colocation data center operator and a portfolio company of Chirisa Investments, which also owns the Piscataway, New Jersey, Richmond, Virginia, and Lynnwood, Washington facilities already on file elsewhere in this registry under the same operator.

reading.body:
Digital Fortress Portland 2 is a 3,500 square foot colocation facility in Beaverton, Oregon with 1.2 megawatts of available IT capacity on an N+1 redundant power configuration and 160 tons of direct expansion cooling. At a typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, 1.2 megawatts of IT load translates to roughly 30 racks, though this facility appears designed for general colocation rather than large-scale GPU clusters. The operator acquired this building and two neighboring Portland facilities from Atmosera in January 2021 and transferred more than 100 colocation customers to Digital Fortress, indicating an active hosting business rather than a greenfield development.

The facility holds SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II certifications and connects to 16 fiber optic carriers and seven subsea cables through membership in the Northwest Access Exchange and the Seattle Internet Exchange. These certifications qualify it for regulated workloads and its carrier count suggests general-purpose colocation connectivity rather than a dedicated hyperscaler backbone. The facility does not publish its total capacity figure, preventing direct assessment of its actual density or utilization.

Portland 2 ranks ninth in published capacity across Oregon, though this ranking reflects only eight facilities in the state that publish megawatt figures out of 133 mapped data centers. Oregon's eight published facilities total 156.6 megawatts, placing this facility at less than 1% of the state's disclosed capacity. The facility is one of three adjacent buildings Digital Fortress operates in the Portland area, but the state context does not distinguish capacity or utilization across these properties.
